results.title: NCB, security forces destroy over 1.37 lakh kg of cannabis plants across 458 acres in Arunachal
results.description: Itanagar, Nov 7 (IANS) The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), in coordination with the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and Arunachal Pradesh Police, destroyed illicit cannabis cultivation spread across approximately 458 acres in West Kameng district of Arunachal Pradesh. The joint operation was conducted in the Kalaktang subdivision of West Kameng in the first phase of the anti-narcotics drive, which took place from October 26 to November 3. During the operation, the teams destroyed more than 1.37 lakh kg of cannabis plants, primarily cultivated on community lands, according to an official press release. The operation was led by the NCB’s Itanagar Zonal Unit and involved 118 personnel and workers, with participation from the SSB, CRPF, Arunachal Pradesh Anti-Narcotics Task Force, West Kameng Police and the district administration. Ground surveys conducted by the West Kameng Police and district administration, along with satellite imagery provided by the NCB, helped identify and locate illicit cultivation sites in the district’s rugged terrain. Custom Ad: Multiplex According to the NCB, the area cleared of illicit cannabis cultivation across Arunachal Pradesh so far in 2026 is more than eight times the total area cleared during the entire year in 2025. The agency has also identified several locations across the state where illicit cannabis and opium poppy are being cultivated. Further joint operations are planned to target these sites as part of the ongoing crackdown on narcotics cultivation. The upcoming drives will also focus on opium poppy cultivation areas in Lohit, Lower Dibang Valley, Dibang Valley, Namsai, Anjaw, Tirap, Changlang and Longding districts. The operation is part of the implementation of the Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026–2029), which calls for mapping illicit cultivation hotspots and coordinating crop destruction activities among central, state and district agencies through a “whole-of-government approach”. The NCB has also undertaken similar operations in other parts of the country. Earlier, an NCB-led drive cleared approximately 592 acres of illicit cannabis cultivation in the Parvati Valley of Kullu district in Himachal Pradesh. In Odisha, the bureau participated in the launch of the state’s ‘Mission Zero Cannabis Cultivation’ initiative in Kandhamal and Boudh districts. Around 30 acres of illicit cannabis cultivation were cleared in Kandhamal as part of the initiative. The NCB has urged members of the public to come forward and report cases of illicit cultivation or drug trafficking. People can share information confidentially through the MANAS National Narcotics Helpline at the toll-free number 1933, the release said. --IANS rs/rad

results.title: 'It was all of us': Khawaja blows whistle on Cape Town sandpaper gate
results.description: New Delhi, Nov 7 (IANS) Former Australian cricketer Usman Khawaja has dropped bombshell claims that the whole Australian team was aware of the infamous sandpaper gate incident during the Cape Town Test in 2018 against South Africa. Khawaja is set to detail his explosive claims in his autobiography 'Sabr' that will be published on Tuesday. However, three days out from the release, the former opener has revealed what the book will carry regarding the incident and that the whole team was aware of the sandpaper's use on the ball in the Cape Town Test. Moreover, he also revealed that the object was used during the previous Test match as well. "It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us," Khawaja said, as quoted by the Sydney Morning Herald. "In an ideal world, I don’t want to do this. I don’t want to be the one who comes out and talks about the truth. The issue is that I genuinely thought after eight years the truth would have been out by now." Until now, the public narrative of the incident was that the then captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were involved in the incident, with Bancroft having applied the object to the ball. Smith and Warner were handed a one-year ban from playing in international and domestic cricket while Bancroft was banned for nine months. Custom Ad: Multiplex Moreover, Smith was told that he could not captain Australia for two years. Warner was hit with a lifetime leadership ban in international and Australian domestic cricket, something which was overturned in 2024. "Maybe I thought Davey would have exposed it, or someone else would have talked about it more. I just didn't think it was going to come down to this. But the longer it's gone on for, and right from the very start, I've been on the train of collectively taking it. "Even in the change rooms, when I was talking to them after the game. I said, 'Take this as a team'. We did this as a team. We knew what was going on, and we have to take it as a team, and so I was always of that stance," he added. He added that the likes of Smith, Bancroft and Warner have been criticised up until now for that act and that the incident led to long-lasting scars on them. "Obviously, it didn't work that way, and those three guys got crucified. "I've seen Davey over the last eight years just get nailed bad over and over again, and it's taken a big man not to say anything and just to stay quiet. "And he's just copped it, and he's copped it, and he's copped it. And then 'Bangers' (Bancroft) in the same note, particularly, he played a little bit of Test cricket after that, but then never came back in, even though he's been scoring a lot of runs. He's been a terrific cricketer for a long time, but I know it's something that hangs over his head. "Even Steve Smith. Steve's lucky, the greatest batsman of my generation. He came back from that, and he's come back as good as he ever was in that first Ashes series, and it's kind of been forgotten for him in some respects. But I know he has never ever forgotten that year and how it all panned out." Khawaja said that he was with Bancroft in the dressing room throughout the match and was never interviewed by Cricket Australia on the incident. "I was sitting next to Cam Bancroft that whole Test match, and I didn't get interviewed," Khawaja said. "I thoroughly feel that I didn't get interviewed because of that, because they knew that I wanted to take it as a team, because they knew I was ready to tell the truth if I was interviewed. "And I was waiting for my phone to ring. It just never rang, and then the penalties were given, and I couldn't believe it." In 2021, Bancroft had stated that it was "self-explanatory" that the bowlers had awareness of the incident in Cape Town, which led to Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon releasing a joint statement denying having any knowledge of the same. Khawaja also claimed that the South African team was "far better" at working with the ball and that they were "trying to keep up with them". He further said that he would reveal what they were doing in his book. Meanwhile, then South Africa captain Faf du Plessis has stated multiple times that his team was also trying to get the ball to reverse through unconventional methods, and he had previously been sanctioned twice for ball tampering. --IANS vm/vi

results.title: 'King' Rules Forever! Virat Kohli Still Evolving at 38 & That's Why He's Really Dangerous
results.description: On November 5, Virat Kohli turned 38. 'King' was not even 20 when he made his debut for India and since 2008, he's been in service to the nation across formats. He left T20Is and Tests in 2024 and 2025 respectively and now plays with a different kind of freedom in ODIs. Kohli's career is on his last legs, but the man is getting better with age as he hopes to sign off with a dream farewell at the 2027 ODI World Cup. 'King' Defies Age with EaseHe had a great 2025 and has had a brilliant 2026 so far. In other words, age is not merely a number for the legend; it's something he defies on a daily basis. But believe it or not, this Kohli is more dangerous than the prime Kohli. Why? Because the man never stops evolving. © X/ICC Virat Kohli Still Growing as a PlayerEven now, at the age of 38, Kohli does not stop learning. Be it making adjustments to his batting or adopting a fresh approach, 'King' is constantly moving with the times. In the last 18 months or so, he has adopted a more aggressive approach. Not that he was a slow batter to begin with, but even by his standards, the man is defying the norm. Kohli may not be the same player he was six to eight years back, but he's not changed for the worse. In fact, the change has been for the better. Why Is This Version of Virat Kohli More Dangerous? This Kohli is more dangerous because of his evolution being constant. The fact that he is no longer one-dimensional makes the bowlers' job harder. When he had one dimension to his game, he was virtually indestructible. So now imagine with multiple dimensions, how lethal he is going to be. Or rather, how lethal he is proving to be. © X/ICC Raising the Bar on Sachin Tendulkar's BenchmarkWhen Kohli first came on the scene and slowly became India's premier batter, the man was hailed as the next Sachin Tendulkar. In time, he proved he was not the next Sachin; he was the first Kohli. Sachin is the benchmark, but Kohli is the one who raised the bar. The fact that he is compared to the 'Master Blaster' shows not only Sachin's greatness but Kohli's worthiness of comparison. Virat Kohli's Evolution Far from OverHe is the twilight of his career, and the end is not far off. The end will come one day, and when Kohli does walk into the sunset, his legacy shall be the benchmark for future batters. But until then, his evolution still continues as he grows as a player. Do not be surprised if the best is yet to come as far as the 'King' is concerned. He is old, but not obsolete.
